Bestow

bih-STOH -- two syllables, stress on the second syllable, STOH. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To bestow is to present a gift or honor.

The town will bestow its medal of valor on the two teenagers who pulled a fisherman from the river.

Worked Example

Every June, the garden club's president saves one moment for last: she calls up the volunteer who logged the most hours and, with great ceremony, bestows the silver trowel upon the winner.

To bestow is to formally present a gift or honor -- and notice the pattern the verb loves: you bestow something upon (or on) someone. It is giving with ceremony in it. You bestow a medal, a title, or an award -- never a stick of gum.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

award: To award is to give a prize that has been won -- judges award medals, committees award scholarships. Bestow needs no contest: it is ceremonial giving, chosen freely by the giver to honor someone.

present: To present is the neutral verb for handing something over in front of others -- you can present a report, a check, or a bouquet. Bestow presents only gifts and honors, and it wraps the giving in ceremony and weight.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

withhold: to deliberately keep something back

deny: to refuse to give something

Where it sits · how ceremonial the giving is — grant → bestow → confer

grant vs. bestow: Grant is the plainer, weaker word -- a wish, a request, or permission can be granted with a nod -- while bestow adds formality and ceremony to the giving.

confer vs. bestow: Confer sits at the far ceremonial end, a step beyond bestow: a university confers degrees and a state confers knighthoods -- official, institutional ceremony -- while bestow keeps a human giver warmly handing the honor across.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — be-

prefix — be-: about, thoroughly (Old English)

root — stow

root — stow: a place (Old English stow)

Put it together

Put it together: Bestow originally meant 'to put in a place' -- be- ('thoroughly') plus stow ('a place'). Over time, placing something valuable into someone's keeping became the word for formally presenting a gift or honor: when you bestow a medal, you place it in worthy hands.

Use the root in a new word: stow

Use the root in a new word: stow: Passengers must stow their bags beneath the seats before takeoff.

Root Check

Word Choice

Bestow is ceremonial giving, and it travels with a preposition: bestow an honor upon (or on) someone. Keep the giver worthy and the gift weighty -- titles, medals, degrees, blessings. For everyday handing-over, use give; nobody bestows a pencil.
